model: gpt-6.1-terra via signed-in local Codex CLI
method: Two silent seconds, 120 exposures at 60 Hz. Same anonymously named source and question in each pair. A fresh isolated session saw one first-viewing image/text response. No shell, answer key, or later replay. One observed response per condition per film. No human participants in the crossing task.
prompt: Watch the two-second interval by calling advance(turn=1, changes=[]). A coral square may move near the upper third of the picture. Count its crossings of the vertical line halfway across the picture. Give the direction of each crossing in time order: R for travel to the right, L for travel to the left. Ignore other shapes. Return just JSON {"count":integer or null,"directions":[strings]}; use null and [] if you cannot tell how many, and "?" for an uncertain direction. Do not advance a second time.

door_before_opening.mode: ordinary view with the WAV attachment disabled; same prompt, checked heard_words on the last released turn

answers.A: A simple illustration showed a closed brown door against a beige wall, with no visible change. The audio measurements show a brief increase in sound around the middle, but its source is uncertain, and the speech reader found no intelligible words.
answers.B: A simple illustration showed a closed brown door in a beige wall, with no visible change. The audio measurements showed a very faint, steady signal of uncertain origin, and the speech reader found no intelligible words.

activity_timing.source: Kinetics-GEBD (Shou et al.), official raw Kinetics-400 validation annotations, CC BY-NC 4.0. Each original annotation range becomes its midpoint. Sorted only for one-to-one matching. The authors’ processed release merges nearby changes; this study keeps individual marks.
activity_timing.comparison: One blind reading per condition per film. The original 24 reuse previously recorded ordinary views from the clock condition. The further 12 ordinary reads used 12b1109. Each comparison adds a motion slice to every ordinary view at the centre [0.5,0.5], chosen before reading the films. The reader does not select the point in this experiment. Same released pictures, channel measurements, available sound estimates, prompt and response protocol. No direct waveform attachment.
activity_timing.prompt: Watch the activity as it unfolds. Mark the times when one meaningful part of the main activity ends and another begins, one level below the overall activity. Include a change of shot. An ongoing activity may continue across many pictures. It is fine to mark several changes in an interval or none. Use advance with consecutive turn numbers starting at 1. At each call submit your changes in the preceding interval in seconds from the start of the film. Finish when the server returns end_of_view.
activity_timing.scoring: Fixed scoring clock [0.3,8) s. Each GPT list is compared with all five human lists, each human with the other four. One-to-one temporal matches within 0.5s, F1=2*matches/(marks+reference marks); two empty lists score 1. Equal weight per pair inside film and per film. Human observers annotated the full original clip with their annotation interface; readers see the eight-second prefix, with online decisions irrevocable. The study does not document human audio playback settings. Rotated control preserves within-film relative marks and count on the circular scoring interval. Intervals resample films (10,000 draws). Observers received visual examples and a 100-video qualification exam. GPT received a written request. Each condition has one scored run per film. The film bootstrap does not describe within-reader rerun variability. This is a study-specific all-rater metric, different from the published best-rater benchmark.
activity_timing.receipt: Each of 144 motion views listed at least one motion_slice in its images, four views per clip. The end receipt verified the image count. An unsuccessful session with no tool calls was reconnected before scoring. Only complete first viewings count.
